name: Personal Current Account Opening
description: A personal customer applies for and successfully opens a personal current account, including digital identity verification, KYC/CDD risk assessment, automated account decisioning, account provisioning, digital channel activation, and initial onboarding communications. This is the foundational journey that establishes the Customer and Account aggregate roots used by all downstream retail journeys. Mandated by the bank's PRA deposit-taking permission and MLR 2017 CDD obligation at onboarding.

phases.name: Application Initiation
phases.description: The customer begins the account opening journey via the mobile app or web portal. Personal details are collected — full name, date of birth, residential address, email, phone number, and nationality. The customer selects the account type (standard current account, packaged account, or switching via CASS). A preliminary eligibility check is run: age (18+), UK residency, existing customer status. An ApplicationStarted domain event is published and a provisional application reference is issued.
phases.governance_notes: Consumer Duty (PS22/9) requires application flow to be clear and not misleading. SCA is not yet required at this pre-authentication stage; a lightweight device fingerprint and fraud signal is captured by SVC-013. Under-18 age check is mandatory — applicants below 18 must be redirected to junior account journey.
entry_conditions: Customer has accessed web portal (CH-001) or mobile app (CH-002)
Customer has confirmed they are aged 18 or over and a UK resident
No pre-existing active personal current account detected for the same identity (deduplication check)
exit_conditions: Personal details form completed and submitted
Preliminary eligibility check passed
ApplicationStarted event published with application_ref assigned
Customer progresses to identity verification (PH-002)
exit_conditions_failure: Applicant is under 18 — redirect to junior account exception path (EX-004)
Applicant is not UK resident — out-of-scope decline with signpost to eligible products
Duplicate identity detected — branch referral or account recovery journey initiated

phases.name: Identity Verification
phases.description: The customer provides identity documents via mobile camera capture or web document upload. The Customer Onboarding Service (SVC-050) orchestrates document authentication (passport, driving licence, or national identity card), biometric liveness check, and address verification. The identity verification vendor (Onfido/Jumio) performs OCR, document authenticity analysis, and biometric matching of the customer's selfie to the photo document. Address is verified against electoral roll, credit bureau, or utility data. An IdentityVerificationCompleted event is published with a pass/fail outcome.
phases.governance_notes: MLR 2017 Regulation 27 mandates CDD completion before establishing a customer relationship. Identity verification must meet JMLSG Part I guidance standards. Biometric data is sensitive personal data under UK GDPR Article 9; explicit consent and a DPIA are required. Branch staff (PER-056) may complete identity verification in branch using manual document check as an eKYC fallback path. Document and biometric data must not be retained beyond the verification event unless required for ongoing CDD obligations.
entry_conditions: ApplicationStarted event received; application_ref valid
Customer has selected supported identity document type
Device camera or file upload capability confirmed (mobile/web)
exit_conditions: Document authenticity check passed
Biometric liveness check passed
Address verification confirmed
IdentityVerificationCompleted event published with outcome: PASS
Customer progresses to KYC/CDD assessment (PH-003)
exit_conditions_failure: Document authentication fails — customer offered one retry with alternative document
Liveness check fails — fraud signal raised; application suspended pending manual review
Identity fraud detection — EX-003 exception path triggered
Address cannot be verified — branch referral path or manual document collection

phases.name: KYC/CDD Assessment
phases.description: The KYC/AML Service (SVC-014) and Sanctions Screening Service (SVC-051) perform automated Customer Due Diligence. This includes: (1) PEP screening — checking the customer's name and date of birth against Politically Exposed Person databases (ComplyAdvantage/Refinitiv World-Check); (2) sanctions screening — real-time check against OFSI Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated List, and EU sanctions lists; (3) adverse media screening — automated search for negative news items associated with the customer; (4) customer risk scoring — algorithmic assignment of a CDD risk tier (Low/Medium/High) based on identity, occupation, source of funds, country of residence, and PEP/adverse media results. KYCClearanceGranted or KYCReferralRaised event is published based on outcome.
phases.governance_notes: MLR 2017 Regulations 27–33 govern CDD requirements. Regulation 33 requires EDD for PEPs. GOV-005-R02 mandates real-time sanctions screening — batch-end screening is not compliant. A sanctions hit must immediately block account opening and escalate to the MLRO (PER-052). GOV-005-R01 prohibits tipping off the customer if a SAR is under consideration. The Starling Bank FCA fine (£29m, October 2024) for incomplete sanctions screening coverage is a direct enforcement signal — screening must cover 100% of applicants.
entry_conditions: IdentityVerificationCompleted event with outcome PASS received
Verified identity data (name, DOB, address, nationality) available to screening services
exit_conditions: PEP/sanctions/adverse media screening returned CLEAR or reviewed
Customer risk score assigned (Low / Medium / High)
KYCClearanceGranted event published for standard (CDD) risk applicants
Customer progresses to account decision (PH-004)
exit_conditions_failure: Sanctions hit detected — SanctionsHitDetected event raised; EX-002 exception path triggered
PEP identified — KYCReferralRaised for EDD; AP-001 alternative path (manual referral with EDD)
High adverse media — risk score escalated to High; manual review required
Automated screening error — SVC-051 degraded mode; application paused with estimated SLA to customer

phases.name: Account Decision
phases.description: An automated account decision engine evaluates the combined output of identity verification, KYC/CDD risk scoring, and basic eligibility checks to produce an Approve, Refer, or Decline decision. Approval criteria include: KYCClearanceGranted, identity PASS, age 18+, UK residency confirmed, and risk score Low or Medium. Refer criteria include: risk score High, PEP status identified (pending EDD), additional manual checks flagged. Decline criteria include: KYC failure, sanctions hit, identity fraud detection, or policy exclusion. An ApplicationDecisionMade domain event is published with the decision, decision basis, and any referral reason.
phases.governance_notes: Consumer Duty (PS22/9) requires that decline decisions are communicated clearly and that customers are signposted to the Financial Ombudsman Service where appropriate. Under FCA Consumer Duty price and value outcome, packaged account fees must be disclosed pre-decision. The decision audit trail (including the decision basis and data inputs) must be retained for minimum 5 years for FCA supervision evidence. AI/ML credit eligibility models used in decisioning must be validated under PRA model risk management standards.
entry_conditions: KYCClearanceGranted event received (or KYCReferralRaised for refer path)
Identity verification outcome PASS confirmed
All mandatory application fields complete
exit_conditions: ApplicationDecisionMade event published with outcome: APPROVED
Customer notified of approval in-app and by email
Customer progresses to account provisioning (PH-005)
exit_conditions_refer: ApplicationDecisionMade event published with outcome: REFERRED
Manual review queue entry created for compliance team
AP-001 (manual referral / EDD) alternative path activated
Customer notified of processing delay with estimated review SLA (max 3 business days)
exit_conditions_decline: ApplicationDecisionMade event published with outcome: DECLINED
Customer notified of decline with reason code; FOS signpost provided
Where KYC failure or sanctions — EX-001 or EX-002 exception paths activated

phases.name: Account Provisioning
phases.description: Upon approval, the Retail Banking Core (SVC-001) creates the account record: assigns a unique sort code and account number from the bank's allocated range (subject to Vocalink/Pay.UK scheme rules), creates the customer ledger record, sets the opening balance to zero, configures account attributes (overdraft limit — initially nil, account type, FSCS eligibility flag), and assigns FSCS depositor protection status. Debit card issuance is triggered via the card processing service (SVC-011/Marqeta/Thredd). The AccountOpened and AccountProvisioned domain events are published. A Single Customer View (SCV) record is created or updated for FSCS compliance.
phases.governance_notes: PRA Depositor Protection rules require the FSCS information sheet to be issued at account opening. The SCV (Single Customer View) file must be maintainable such that FSCS could extract the customer's eligible deposit data within 24 hours of a payout trigger. CASS participation requires the sort code and account number to be registered with Pay.UK within 2 business days of account opening. Card issuance must comply with PCI DSS v4.0 and Visa/Mastercard scheme rules. The CardIssuanceTriggered event initiates the physical card production and dispatch workflow (typically 3–5 working days for delivery).
entry_conditions: ApplicationDecisionMade event with outcome APPROVED received
Sort code and account number range available for allocation
Customer identity and address records confirmed in SCV
exit_conditions: Account record created on SVC-001 with sort code, account number, and opening balance
AccountOpened domain event published
CardIssuanceTriggered event published to card processing service
SCV record created/updated with new account
CASS registration initiated with Pay.UK
Customer progresses to digital channel activation (PH-006)
exit_conditions_failure: Sort code/account number allocation failure — IT Operations (PER-060) alerted; EX-005 provisioning failure path
SCV update failure — FSCS compliance alert raised; manual correction required before card issuance

phases.name: Digital Channel Activation
phases.description: The customer sets up online and mobile banking access. This phase covers: (1) credential creation — the customer sets their online banking username and password; (2) biometric enrolment — the customer enrolls a biometric factor (Face ID, Touch ID, or Android BiometricPrompt) as the SCA inherence factor bound to the device via FIDO2/WebAuthn; (3) device registration — the device is registered as the customer's primary SCA possession factor via SVC-100 (Identity & Access Management); (4) notification preferences — push notification permissions are configured via SVC-053; (5) first login verification — the customer completes a first-login authentication using SCA (password + biometric) to confirm channel activation. A DigitalChannelActivated domain event is published.
phases.governance_notes: SCA enrolment must comply with PSR 2017 Regulation 100 and FCA RTS on SCA. Biometric data enrolled for authentication is sensitive personal data under UK GDPR Article 9; the processing must be based on explicit consent and a DPIA must be on file. The enrolled biometric must not be shared with third parties without further explicit consent. Under FIDO2/WebAuthn, the biometric template never leaves the device — only the cryptographic assertion is transmitted to SVC-100, satisfying UK GDPR data minimisation.
entry_conditions: AccountProvisioned event received; account number and sort code confirmed
Customer has access to the mobile app (CH-002) or web portal (CH-001)
Card issuance triggered (card delivery does not block channel activation)
exit_conditions: Online banking credentials created and stored (hashed) in SVC-100
Biometric SCA factor enrolled and device registered
Push notifications enabled
First-login SCA authentication completed
DigitalChannelActivated event published
Customer progresses to welcome and onboarding (PH-007)
exit_conditions_failure: Biometric enrolment fails — customer offered TOTP app as alternative SCA factor
Device registration fails — IT Operations (PER-060) alerted; customer directed to contact support

phases.name: Welcome and Onboarding
phases.description: Following digital channel activation, the customer receives a structured welcome and onboarding experience. This includes: (1) welcome communication — a welcome pack (email and in-app message) confirming account details, sort code/account number, card dispatch date, and FSCS protection status; (2) initial funding prompt — an in-app prompt to transfer opening funds or set up salary payment to the new account, with CASS switching options displayed where eligible; (3) product cross-sell presentation — contextually appropriate product introductions (linked savings account, overdraft facility eligibility, or packaged account upgrade) presented in compliance with Consumer Duty consumer understanding obligations; (4) vulnerability screening — brief wellbeing questions surfaced in-app to identify potential vulnerability indicators, consistent with FCA FG21/1. A WelcomePackDispatched event is published.
phases.governance_notes: Consumer Duty (PS22/9) consumer understanding outcome requires that all communications are clear, fair, and not misleading. The FSCS information sheet and exclusions list must be provided at account opening (GOV-001-R02). Cross-sell presentations must comply with Consumer Duty products and services outcome — only appropriate products for the customer's likely target market may be presented. Vulnerability indicators captured in this phase must be recorded in the customer record and reflected in subsequent interactions per FCA FG21/1.
entry_conditions: DigitalChannelActivated event received
Account is fully operational (sort code, account number confirmed)
Customer is authenticated in mobile app or web portal
exit_conditions: Welcome pack sent via email and in-app notification
FSCS information sheet delivered
Initial funding prompt displayed
CASS switching option presented where applicable
WelcomePackDispatched event published
Journey complete — customer is an active account holder

happy_path.description: A UK resident individual aged 18+ applies via mobile app, passes digital identity verification first time, receives a CLEAR PEP/sanctions result with a Low risk score, is automatically approved, has their account provisioned, activates digital banking with biometric SCA, and receives their welcome communications. Full journey completes in under 10 minutes for the automated path.

alternative_paths.name: Manual Referral — EDD Required
alternative_paths.description: Triggered when KYC/CDD assessment returns a High risk score, PEP identification, or adverse media hit that cannot be automatically cleared. Application is placed into a manual review queue. A Compliance Officer reviews the application, requests additional source of funds/wealth documentation from the customer (delivered via secure document upload in the app), and performs Enhanced Due Diligence per MLR 2017 Regulation 33. MLRO (PER-052) sign-off required for PEP approvals. If EDD is satisfied, the journey resumes at PH-004 (Account Decision) with a manual approval. Target review SLA: 3 business days.
alternative_paths.regulatory_basis: MLR 2017 Regulations 33–35 (EDD for PEPs and high-risk customers)
alternative_paths.sla: 3 business days for EDD review and decision

alternative_paths.name: Joint Account Application
alternative_paths.description: Two applicants apply for a joint personal current account. Both applicants must complete identity verification (PH-002) and KYC/CDD assessment (PH-003) independently. Both must receive a positive KYC outcome before the account decision (PH-004) is triggered. FSCS protection applies at £85,000 per account holder (i.e., £85,000 each in a two-person joint account). Account provisioning (PH-005) creates a joint account record with two authorised signatories. Both parties must complete digital channel activation (PH-006) independently.
alternative_paths.trigger: Customer selects 'Joint Account' at application initiation (PH-001)
alternative_paths.sla: Dependent on both applicants completing KYC; second applicant invited within 2 business days

alternative_paths.name: Account Switching via CASS
alternative_paths.description: An existing customer at another bank initiates a Current Account Switch Service (CASS) transfer as part of or immediately following account opening. The customer authorises the switch in-app using the CASS switch form. The CASS service orchestrates the redirection of Direct Debits, standing orders, and incoming payments from the old account over a 7-working-day switching window. The old account is closed by the previous bank on the Switch Date. The bank must register the new account with Pay.UK CASS and guarantee the 7-working-day SLA as a CASS participant.
alternative_paths.trigger: Customer selects 'Switch my account' at PH-001 or PH-007 welcome phase
alternative_paths.regulatory_basis: CAP-001 mandate: Current Account Switch Service (CASS) rules — Pay.UK
alternative_paths.sla: Switch must complete within 7 working days of Switch Date (CASS guarantee)

exception_paths.name: KYC Failure — SAR Consideration
exception_paths.description: Where identity verification or KYC/CDD assessment reveals information that gives the bank reasonable grounds to suspect money laundering or terrorist financing, the application is declined and the case is referred to the MLRO (PER-052) for SAR assessment. The MLRO must decide within 5 business days whether to submit a Suspicious Activity Report to the NCA UKFIU (POCA 2002 s330). The tipping-off prohibition (POCA 2002 s333A) applies — the customer must not be informed that a SAR has been or may be filed. The customer receives a standard decline notification without disclosure of the SAR consideration.
exception_paths.trigger: Identity verification failure with fraud indicators, or CDD assessment revealing ML/TF suspicion
exception_paths.sla: MLRO SAR decision within 5 business days of suspicion being formed

exception_paths.name: Sanctions Hit — Account Freeze and MLRO Escalation
exception_paths.description: Where sanctions screening (SVC-051) returns a confirmed match against the OFSI Consolidated List or other designated lists, the application is immediately blocked. No account may be opened and no funds may be accepted. The SanctionsHitDetected event triggers immediate escalation to the MLRO (PER-052). The MLRO must notify OFSI within 14 days of confirming that a customer is a designated person (GOV-005-R02). Any funds already received must be frozen. The customer is not informed of the specific reason for the block (tipping-off prohibition). Voluntary disclosure to OFSI may be required.
exception_paths.trigger: SanctionsHitDetected event from SVC-051 during PH-003
exception_paths.regulatory_basis: GOV-005-R02; UK Financial Sanctions legislation; OFSI regulations; POCA 2002 s333A (tipping off)
exception_paths.sla: OFSI notification within 14 days of confirmed designated person identification

exception_paths.name: Identity Fraud Detection
exception_paths.description: Where the identity verification service (SVC-050 / Onfido / Jumio) detects document tampering, synthetic identity indicators, or biometric spoofing, the application is suspended and a fraud alert is raised to the Fraud Analyst team (PER-054). The application is declined and a fraud case is created in the fraud case management system. The device fingerprint and application metadata are retained as fraud investigation evidence. Where the fraud involves a stolen identity, the legitimate identity owner may need to be notified via a separate process.
exception_paths.trigger: IdentityVerificationCompleted event with outcome FRAUD_DETECTED from SVC-050
exception_paths.regulatory_basis: GOV-005-R03 (failure to prevent fraud); MLR 2017 CDD obligations; FCA APP fraud prevention
exception_paths.sla: Fraud case created and reviewed within 1 business day

exception_paths.name: Under-18 Applicant — Junior Account Redirect
exception_paths.description: Where the applicant's date of birth indicates they are under 18, the personal current account application cannot proceed (regulatory requirement and bank policy). The applicant is redirected to the junior/young person account application journey with appropriate parental consent requirements. A clear, friendly in-app message explains the redirect and the available junior account options.
exception_paths.trigger: Age check at PH-001 returns age < 18
exception_paths.regulatory_basis: Consumer Credit Act 1974 capacity rules; bank policy minimum age for current account

exception_paths.name: Account Provisioning Failure
exception_paths.description: Where the Retail Banking Core (SVC-001) fails to create the account record (e.g. sort code allocation failure, system outage, duplicate account number conflict), IT Operations (PER-060) are alerted via the observability platform (SVC-112). The customer is notified that their application was approved but account activation is delayed, with a committed resolution SLA. The account decision and KYC results are preserved so provisioning can be retried without re-running KYC. Operational resilience obligations under PRA SS1/21 apply — provisioning is part of the Important Business Service for account opening.
exception_paths.trigger: AccountProvisioned event failure or timeout from SVC-001 during PH-005
exception_paths.regulatory_basis: PRA SS1/21 operational resilience; FCA PS21/3 important business service obligations
exception_paths.sla: Resolution within 4 business hours for standard provisioning failure; 1 business day maximum
